```{r cran-gate, include = FALSE}

EVAL_FITS <- identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true")
```

Each entry below starts from a situation, shows the message tulpa prints in
that situation, and ends on a corrected call that runs. The entries are
grouped by the stage at which the message appears: preparing the input,
setting priors and the dispersion, fitting, and reading how reliable a fit is.
The terms used here (control knob, tier, outer grid, Pareto k) are defined in
[Concepts](concepts.html). Installation is covered in
[Get started](tulpa.html).

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(tulpa)
```

## Example data

Every entry uses the data below. `d` holds 300 Gaussian measurements on 12
groups `g`, simulated from an intercept of 0.5, a slope of 1.2 on `x`, group
offsets with standard deviation 0.6 and residual standard deviation 0.8. `db`
holds a binary response on the same `x` and `g`, and `dc` a count of successes
out of 5 trials. `ds` places binary observations in 10 regions on a ring, with
the adjacency matrix `W`, and adds a time index `time` and a three-level panel
factor `site`.

```{r data}
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
g <- factor(sample(1:12, n, replace = TRUE))
u <- rnorm(12, sd = 0.6)
d  <- data.frame(y = 0.5 + 1.2 * x + u[g] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8), x = x, g = g)
db <- data.frame(y = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.3 + x + u[g])), x = x, g = g)
dc <- data.frame(y = rbinom(n, 5, plogis(-0.3 + x)), x = x)

K <- 10
W <- matrix(0, K, K)
for (i in 1:K) { j <- if (i < K) i + 1 else 1; W[i, j] <- W[j, i] <- 1 }
ds <- data.frame(y = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.2 + 0.7 * x)), x = x,
                 region = sample(1:K, n, replace = TRUE),
                 time = sample(1:15, n, replace = TRUE),
                 site = factor(sample(1:3, n, replace = TRUE)))
```

## Input

### A tuning setting passed as an argument

`n_threads`, `n_iter`, `max_iter` and the other settings that change how the
computation runs are not arguments of `tulpa()`. Given as one, the fit stops
before any work and says where the setting goes.

```{r knob-dots, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace",
      phi = 0.8^2, n_threads = 2)
```

Move it into `control`.

```{r knob-dots-fix}
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace",
             phi = 0.8^2, control = list(n_threads = 2))
coef(fit)
```

### A misspelled control knob

A name in `control` that no backend reads is refused, and the message lists
every name `tulpa()` accepts.

```{r knob-typo, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace",
      phi = 0.8^2, control = list(n_thread = 2))
```

The list is long because it covers every backend; the fix is the spelling
`n_threads` used in the previous entry.

### A knob the chosen backend does not read

Once `mode` is fixed, `control` is checked against the backend that will run.
A Laplace fit has no chain, so a chain length is refused, and the message
lists the three knobs the Laplace backend reads.

```{r knob-backend, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace",
      sigma_re = 0.6, phi = 0.8^2, control = list(n_iter = 2000))
```

Either drop the knob or pick a backend that reads it. `n_iter` and `warmup`
belong to the samplers.

```{r knob-backend-fix}
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "mala",
             sigma_re = 0.6, phi = 0.8^2,
             control = list(n_iter = 2000, warmup = 500))
coef(fit)
```

### A variable the data do not contain

A covariate missing from `data` stops the fit with R's own message. A missing
grouping variable is named by tulpa.

```{r missing-var, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ z, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace", phi = 0.8^2)
tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | h), data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace",
      phi = 0.8^2)
```

Check `names(d)` against every variable in the formula, including the one
after the bar.

```{r missing-var-fix}
names(d)
coef(tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "gaussian",
           mode = "laplace", sigma_re = 0.6, phi = 0.8^2))
```

### Binomial counts without the number of trials

`dc$y` counts successes out of 5. Without `n_trials`, `binomial` expects a 0/1
response and stops.

```{r trials, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x, data = dc, family = "binomial", mode = "laplace")
```

Pass the trials, one per row.

```{r trials-fix}
coef(tulpa(y ~ x, data = dc, family = "binomial", mode = "laplace",
           n_trials = rep(5, n)))
```

The slope is close to the 1 the counts were simulated with.
[Data formatting](data-formatting.html) shows the other response encodings.

### Missing values in the response

A missing response value stops a Laplace fit, and the message counts the
rows and names the path that reads them: on the nested-Laplace path a row with
no response is a forecast, with its likelihood term masked.

```{r na, error = TRUE}
dna <- d
dna$y[3] <- NA
tulpa(y ~ x, data = dna, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace", phi = 0.8^2)
```

A model with no latent field has no nested-Laplace path (see
[Nested Laplace on a model with no latent field](#nested-laplace-on-a-model-with-no-latent-field)),
so remove the incomplete rows, or impute them, before fitting.

```{r na-fix}
coef(tulpa(y ~ x, data = dna[!is.na(dna$y), ], family = "gaussian",
           mode = "laplace", phi = 0.8^2))
```

### Region codes that do not match the adjacency

An integer region code is a row of the adjacency matrix. `W` has 10 rows, so
codes 11 and 12 point outside it.

```{r adj-range, error = TRUE}
ds_bad <- ds
ds_bad$region[1:2] <- c(11, 12)
tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds_bad, family = "binomial",
      spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W), mode = "laplace")
```

An adjacency with a one-sided link is refused too. `check_adjacency()` reports
every property the spatial fit needs, and flags the asymmetry here.

```{r adj-sym}
W_bad <- W
W_bad[1, 2] <- 0
check_adjacency(W_bad)
```

With codes in `1:10` and the symmetric `W`, the fit runs.

```{r adj-fix}
fit_sp <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",
                spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
                mode = "laplace")
coef(fit_sp)
```

## Priors and dispersion

### A penalised-complexity prior with an invalid tail probability

A penalised-complexity (PC) prior on a standard deviation is set by two
numbers: a scale `U` and the probability `alpha` that the standard deviation
exceeds it. The prior exists only for `U > 0` and `alpha` strictly between 0
and 1, and each constructor that takes the pair checks it.

```{r pc, error = TRUE}
prior_pc(U = 1, alpha = 1.5)
spatial_gp(~ lon + lat, approx = "hsgp", sigma_prior_alpha = 1)
```

`alpha = 0.05` with `U = 1` reads "a 5% prior probability that the standard
deviation exceeds 1".

```{r pc-fix}
prior_pc(U = 1, alpha = 0.05)
```

[Priors](priors.html) covers how to choose `U` and `alpha`.

### A Gaussian fit without `phi`

For `gaussian`, `phi` is the residual variance, and `mode = "laplace"` and
the samplers hold it fixed at the value passed. Left out, it is fixed at 1
with a warning.

```{r phi}
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "laplace")
```

When the residual variance is known, pass it as a variance: here `0.8^2`, not
`0.8`. When it is not known and the model has a random effect,
`mode = "eb"` with `estimate_phi = TRUE` estimates it along with the
random-effect standard deviation.

```{r phi-fix}
fit_eb <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "gaussian",
                mode = "eb", estimate_phi = TRUE)
VarCorr(fit_eb)
```

Both standard deviations are labelled `estimated`: 0.48 for the groups and
0.79 for the residual, against the 0.6 and 0.8 the data were simulated with.

## Fitting

### A combination `tulpa()` does not fit yet

Some combinations of terms are refused before fitting. A random slope next to
a spatial field is one.

```{r combo-slope, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site) + spatial(region), data = ds,
      family = "binomial", spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W))
```

A temporal field with one trend per panel group (`group_var`) next to a
spatial field is another.

```{r combo-panel, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",
      spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
      temporal = temporal_rw1("time", group_var = "site"))
```

Each message names the combination that does fit. With a random intercept in
place of the slope, the spatial model runs.

```{r combo-fix}
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | site) + spatial(region), data = ds,
             family = "binomial",
             spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
             mode = "laplace", sigma_re = 0.5)
coef(fit)
```

### Nested Laplace on a model with no latent field

`mode = "nested_laplace"` integrates the hyperparameters of a spatial,
temporal, smooth or custom field. A model with only a random intercept has
none of these, and the message names the modes that fit it.

```{r nl-none, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
      mode = "nested_laplace")
```

`mode = "structured"` stays in Tier 2 and integrates the random-effect
standard deviation.

```{r nl-none-fix}
fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
             mode = "structured")
c(backend = fit$backend, tier = fit$inference_tier)
```

### An outer grid larger than the cap

A model with a spatial and a temporal field has two hyperparameters, and its
outer grid crosses the two axes, one inner solve per cell.
`control$max_grid_cells` caps the cell count, and a grid past the cap is
refused before any solve, with the axes that produced the count.

```{r grid-cap, error = TRUE}
tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",
      spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
      temporal = temporal_rw1("time"),
      control = list(max_grid_cells = 50, n_threads = 2))
```

Raise the cap above the count the message gives, or leave it unset.
`?tulpa_nested_laplace` documents that an unset cap solves a grid of any size
and warns first when it passes 2048 cells.

```{r grid-cap-fix}
fit_st <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",
                spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
                temporal = temporal_rw1("time"),
                control = list(max_grid_cells = 100, n_threads = 2,
                               progress = FALSE))
coef(fit_st)
```

## Reliability

### A sampler chain that has not converged

A sampler fit checks its own chain. A short chain on the binary data leaves
too few effective draws, and the fit warns, naming the parameters and their
Rhat and bulk effective sample size.

```{r chain}
fit_short <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
                   mode = "mala", sigma_re = 0.6,
                   control = list(n_iter = 150, warmup = 30))
check_diagnostics(fit_short)
```

`check_diagnostics()` lists the checks that failed. A longer chain clears
them.

```{r chain-fix}
fit_long <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
                  mode = "mala", sigma_re = 0.6,
                  control = list(n_iter = 3000, warmup = 1000))
check_diagnostics(fit_long)
head(diagnostics(fit_long), 2)
```

### `diagnostics()` returns nothing for a Laplace fit

A plain Laplace fit computes no reliability quantity, so `diagnostics()`
returns `NULL` with a message.

```{r diag-laplace}
fit_lap <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
                 mode = "laplace", sigma_re = 0.6)
diagnostics(fit_lap)
```

`mode = "imh_laplace"` reuses the Laplace Gaussian as the proposal of an exact
Metropolis-Hastings sampler. A high acceptance rate says the Laplace
approximation was close to the posterior, and the fit then carries a chain
that `diagnostics()` reads.

```{r diag-laplace-fix}
fit_imh <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = db, family = "binomial",
                 mode = "imh_laplace", sigma_re = 0.6)
round(fit_imh$mean_accept, 2)
rbind(laplace = coef(fit_lap), imh = coef(fit_imh))
```

### Reading the reliability report of a nested-Laplace fit

On a nested-Laplace fit `diagnostics()` prints the reliability of the outer
integration over the hyperparameters, and of the inner Laplace layer where
the backend scores it. The fit below puts a random walk over the 15 time
points of `ds`.

```{r diag-read}
fit_rw <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = ds, family = "binomial",
                temporal = temporal_rw1("time"),
                control = list(n_threads = 2))
diagnostics(fit_rw)
```

The lines to read, in order:

- `outer PSIS pareto_k` with its band in parentheses: below 0.5 is good,
  0.5 to 0.7 ok, 0.7 and above unreliable.
- `outer grid quadrature ESS`: how many cells carry the weight. A value near 1
  means a single cell holds the posterior.
- the `note:` lines, which name an axis whose grid was moved or is coarser
  than its posterior.
- `whole-fit verdict`, which combines the outer and inner layers.

Here the outer k is 0.645, in the ok band, and the verdict reads the outer
integration as borderline. Each number is also an attribute of the returned
object. On the two-field fit `fit_st` of the grid entry the outer k is `NA`,
because it is not defined on a multi-block grid, and that fit's verdict says
the outer integration was not assessed.

```{r diag-read-st}
attr(diagnostics(fit_rw), "pareto_k")
attr(diagnostics(fit_st), "pareto_k")
```

[Reliability diagnostics](reliability-pareto-k.html) explains what a k in the
ok or unreliable band means and the levers for it.
